description: Semantic roles, collision tables, epistemic markers, and quantifier precision for the STE-Code linguistic flavor.

semantic_roles.description: Every approved verb maps to a role class. Role violations are the most common STE-Code error class.

Action.description: Verbs that name an operation. Permitted in imperative position. Prohibited as nouns.
Action.rule: Action terms must not appear as nouns. 'The build takes five minutes' → 'The build (n) takes five minutes.' (Exception: 'deploy' resolves to 'deploy (n)' per its term_table entry.)

Result.description: Nouns naming the outcome of an Action. Permitted as nouns. The canonical form for what an Action produces.
Result.rule: Use Result form when naming the output. 'After the build completes' → 'After the build process completes' or restructure. Note: 'deploy' is a resolved exception — the adapted rules use 'the deploy' as the noun form, so its Result is 'deploy (n)' (not 'deployment').

Entity.description: Nouns naming system components, data structures, or concepts. No Action/Result ambiguity.
Entity.rule: Entities must not be verbed. 'Database the records' → 'Store the records in the database.'

Property.description: Adjectives or states describing Entities. Used attributively or predicatively.
Property.rule: Properties are technical adjectives. Comparative forms prohibited — use specific state names.

build.grounding_note: Dual-category term per Rule 1.13:258. Previous ref to 1.7 was wrong — 1.7 has 0 mentions of 'build'.

compile.grounding_note: CONTRADICTION RESOLVED: Rule 1.13:248,276 explicitly states 'compile' is NOT a dual-category word and has no approved noun form. Previous 'compilation' result form removed.

test.grounding_note: Dual-category per Rule 1.13:260. Rule 5.3 uses in compound nouns but doesn't classify.

run.grounding_note: Confirmed at Rule 1.3:59 — 'execute a program or command'.

install.grounding_note: Rule 5.1 uses 'installation' as noun. Imperative form confirmed at Rule 5.3:48.

configure.grounding_note: Previous ref to 1.9 was wrong — 1.9 only has 'configuration' as noun. Verb 'configure' confirmed at Rule 5.3:48.

validate.grounding_note: NOVEL — no counterpart found in any adapted rule. Previous ref to 3.7 was wrong (0 mentions).

commit.grounding_note: Used as verb in Rule 1.7 examples (lines 245, 449) but not explicitly classified as Action term.

migrate.grounding_note: Only noun form 'migration' appears in rule 5.4. Verb 'migrate' implied but never explicitly used.

deploy.grounding_note: CONTRADICTION RESOLVED: Rules use 'deploy' as noun form (Rule 1.13:248 'the deploy is correct'). Previous 'deployment' result form changed to 'deploy (n)' to match rules.

single_referent_rule.description: Every noun phrase must resolve to exactly one entity within its scope. When a term names different things in different sections, the section heading provides the qualifier.
single_referent_rule.precedence: Applied AFTER semantic role check, BEFORE scope bracketing.
qualification_rules: When a head noun appears in multiple contexts, qualify on first use per section: 'the deployment pipeline' vs 'the deployment artifact'.
Qualifier resets at section boundary (### heading or higher).
Pronouns (it, they, this, these) must resolve within one sentence. Cross-sentence pronouns → violation.

domain_collisions.description: Head nouns that name different entities depending on context. Each entry lists the contexts and their qualifier members.

contexts.meaning: the CI job that runs builds

epistemic.description: Every performance, reliability, or scale claim must be classified as Specified, Measured, or Expected.

Specified.example: The endpoint returns a JSON object.
Specified.rule: Permitted for functional behavior. Forbidden for performance/reliability/scale claims.

Measured.example: p99 latency is 87 ms (load test, 2026-07, 10k rps).
Measured.rule: Required for all performance claims. Must carry date or version. Expires after two major versions.

Expected.marker: is expected to / is designed to
Expected.example: The cache is designed to hold 10,000 entries.
Expected.rule: Use for design targets. 'Should' is banned — use 'is designed to' or 'is expected to'.

permitted_modals.may: User optionality only: 'You may omit the token.'
permitted_modals.can: Capability statements: 'The system can process 1000 requests per second.' (requires Measured if performance claim)

bare_performance.good: The API responds with p99 latency of 87 ms (load test, 2026-07, 10k rps).

bare_reliability.good: The system is designed to handle 10,000 concurrent connections.

modal_prediction.bad: The server will retry the request.

bare_scale.good: The database scales to 500 write transactions per second (benchmark, v3.2, 16 vCPU).

lifecycle.description: Term lifecycle tracking for deprecation and graduation.

states.current: Approved for use now. Default state.
states.emerging: In use in corpus, not yet approved. Informational — candidate for graduation.
